Prompt 1 — Fix auth 401 client-side timing (CRITICAL)
The API routes now correctly return 401, but client pages may fire fetches before the NextAuth session cookie is available on mount.

In Infusion Studio v4, users are still being redirected to /login when clicking their own blends and ingredients even though the API routes correctly return 401. The root cause is likely a fetch firing before the session is hydrated.
Fix the following:
1. In src/components/blends/blend-detail-view.tsx — wrap the fetchBlend call in a session check. Import { useSession } from 'next-auth/react'. Add const { status } = useSession(). In the useEffect, add: if (status === 'loading') return; before the fetch. This ensures the fetch only fires once the session cookie is confirmed present.
2. Apply the same pattern to src/components/ingredients/ingredient-detail-view.tsx — add useSession() status check before the load() call in useEffect.
3. In src/app/(dashboard)/dashboard/page.tsx — add useSession() guard before the /api/dashboard fetch.
4. In src/app/(dashboard)/blends/page.tsx and src/app/(dashboard)/ingredients/page.tsx — same pattern: import useSession, check status !== 'loading' before fetching.
5. For the offline APK where useSession is not available (SKIP_AUTH=true or isOfflineDemo), skip the session check entirely — wrap with: if (!isOfflineDemo() && status === 'loading') return;
Test by: hard-refreshing the page while logged in and clicking a user-created blend — it should load correctly without flashing to /login.
